stated_limitation: Two caveats are worth stating. The preferred directions recovered from the continuous velocity model only broadly agree with those from the trial-level cosine fits (circular r = 0.58, median absolute difference about 36 degrees); the two measures are computed from different trial sets and different time windows, so exact agreement was not expected, but the scatter is larger than the classical picture of a single fixed preferred direction would suggest. And the lead time of spiking over the hand is not a single number: the population optimum on moving bins is 80 ms, while single-unit optima are spread over the whole range scanned, with one cluster at the negative edge.

justification.dataset: DANDI 000128 MC_Maze (Jenkins M1/PMd delayed reaching) is the canonical dataset for reach direction and velocity tuning in motor cortex.
justification.handling: Data streamed via remfile, reach direction measured from the hand itself, explicit active-unit (>0.5 Hz) and moving-bin (>50 mm/s) criteria, and the M1/PMd non-separability of the NLB packaging is disclosed.
justification.analysis: Cosine fits with a permutation null, cross-validated Poisson GLMs comparing five feature sets, a lead-time scan, and a ridge decoder together constitute a correct and well-controlled treatment.
justification.correctness: Every headline value (85% tuned, median cosine R²=0.79, GLM pseudo-R² ordering, 80 ms lead, decoder R²=0.67/0.51, 18° error) reproduces from the committed logs and is internally consistent.
justification.figures: Figures are clearly labeled with units and sample sizes, examples are chosen by tuning strength (depth × R², not fitted slope), and each claimed effect is directly visible.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate: the small absolute pseudo-R² is explained rather than hidden, and the write-up names specific limitations (PD scatter, non-unique lead time) plainly.
